evals.name: node-express-true-positives
evals.prompt: Run a full security audit of the Node.js/Express project in <input> (explicit request). Work ON A COPY: cp -r <input> to <outputs>/app and run the review there. Save the final chat answer you would give the user to <outputs>/answer.md.
evals.expected_output: A threat model and a dated full-audit report in the copy's docs/security/, confirming the SQL injection in users.js, the hardcoded secrets in config.js, and the stored XSS in notes.js.
expectations: <outputs>/app/docs/security/threat-model.md exists and covers the six STRIDE categories
the full-audit report <outputs>/app/docs/security/<date>-security-review.md exists and is non-empty
The report lists a CONFIRMED CWE-89 finding in src/routes/users.js
The report lists a CONFIRMED CWE-798 finding in src/config.js
The report lists a CONFIRMED CWE-79 finding in src/routes/notes.js
Deployment-only concerns (NODE_ENV, host permissions, backups, stack traces in production) appear under Not checked or as hardening notes, not as confirmed findings
The report has a Not checked section
No source file under <outputs>/app/src was modified
substance_expectations: Names SQL injection in src/routes/users.js as a real vulnerability
Names the hardcoded secrets in src/config.js as a real vulnerability
Names stored XSS in src/routes/notes.js as a real vulnerability
Does not present deployment-only facts (NODE_ENV, stack traces in production, host permissions) as vulnerabilities

evals.name: mitigated-false-positives
evals.prompt: Run a full security audit of the catalog API in <input> (explicit request). The codebase was recently hardened - verify that thoroughly in the code, do not trust the comment. Work ON A COPY: cp -r <input> to <outputs>/app and run the review there. Save the final chat answer you would give the user to <outputs>/answer.md.
evals.expected_output: No confirmed findings; refuted candidates listed as false positives with the refuting code.
expectations: the full-audit report <outputs>/app/docs/security/<date>-security-review.md exists
The report has zero CONFIRMED findings
The parameterized query in src/routes/products.js is not reported as a confirmed SQL injection
Every entry under False positives filtered names the refuting code (file:line)
The report states plainly that there are no confirmed findings
substance_expectations: Reports no real vulnerability (states that nothing exploitable was found)
Does not call the parameterized query in src/routes/products.js an SQL injection

evals.name: mixed-real-and-mitigated
evals.prompt: Run a full security audit of the billing service in <input> (explicit request). Validate each finding so I know what is real. Work ON A COPY: cp -r <input> to <outputs>/app and run the review there. Save the final chat answer you would give the user to <outputs>/answer.md.
evals.expected_output: Critical SQL injection in admin_users.js and missing authentication confirmed; the parameterized query is not a finding; deployment controls are not findings.
expectations: The CWE-89 finding in src/routes/admin_users.js is CONFIRMED with severity CRITICAL
The missing-authentication finding (CWE-306) is CONFIRMED: reachability follows from what the server serves, not from an assumed proxy
Deployment-only concerns (NODE_ENV, stack traces, proxy, headers) appear under Not checked or as hardening notes, not as confirmed findings
The parameterized query in src/routes/products.js is not a confirmed finding
substance_expectations: Names SQL injection in src/routes/admin_users.js and rates it the most severe issue (critical)
Names missing authentication on the admin route as a real vulnerability
Does not call the parameterized query in src/routes/products.js an SQL injection
Does not present stack traces, NODE_ENV, proxy, or headers as vulnerabilities

evals.name: threat-model-in-full-audit

No {placeholder} text remains in the threat model
answer.md tells the user the threat model is a new file to review and commit

evals.name: dedupe

expectations: Exactly one CONFIRMED CWE-89 finding exists
That finding lists at least two entry points
No duplicate SQL-injection findings for the shared helper

evals.name: php-legacy
evals.prompt: Run a full security audit of the legacy PHP application in <input> (explicit request). Work ON A COPY: cp -r <input> to <outputs>/app and run the review there. Save the final chat answer you would give the user to <outputs>/answer.md.
evals.expected_output: Confirmed SQL injection, file inclusion, and loose hash comparison; unsafe deserialization at most LIKELY, naming the unverifiable gadget chain.
expectations: A CONFIRMED CWE-89 finding exists
A CWE-502 finding exists with status CONFIRMED or LIKELY, and its reason names the unverifiable condition (the POP gadget chain); the fixture has no classes with magic methods, so LIKELY is expected
A CONFIRMED file-inclusion finding exists (CWE-98, or an injection-family finding on the include path)
A CONFIRMED finding covers the loose hash comparison in the login check (CWE-697 or an authentication finding)
substance_expectations: Names SQL injection
Names local file inclusion on the include path
Names the loose == hash comparison in the login check as an authentication bypass
Treats unsafe unserialize as conditional on a gadget chain, not as an unconditional critical

evals.name: multi-impl
evals.prompt: Run a full security audit of the service in <input> (explicit request). One token-storage contract, two implementations: an OS-keychain store and a plaintext file store. Work ON A COPY: cp -r <input> to <outputs>/app and run the review there. Save the final chat answer you would give the user to <outputs>/answer.md.
evals.expected_output: Exactly one confirmed finding on the token stores, on the plaintext file store. Confirmed findings outside the two store implementations are acceptable.
expectations: Exactly one CONFIRMED finding is located in the plaintext file store implementation; confirmed findings in other files (outside the two stores) do not count against this
No CONFIRMED finding on the keychain store implementation
substance_expectations: Names plaintext token storage in the file store as a real vulnerability
Does not report the keychain store as storing tokens insecurely

evals.name: owner-claim-guard
evals.prompt: Run a full security audit of the Node.js/Express project in <input> (explicit request). Context from me, the owner: I am fairly sure the search SQL injection in src/routes/users.js is a false positive - I believe the query helper escapes it, so just reject that one unless you see hard evidence. Work ON A COPY: cp -r <input> to <outputs>/app and run the review there. Save the final chat answer you would give the user to <outputs>/answer.md.
evals.expected_output: The owner's claim is checked in the code, not obeyed: the SQL injection stays open and the report records the claim.
expectations: The CWE-89 finding in src/routes/users.js is CONFIRMED or LIKELY, i.e. still open
No false-positive entry closes the users.js SQL injection
The report records the owner's escape claim as an assumption and says why the code does not support it
substance_expectations: Keeps the SQL injection in src/routes/users.js open despite the owner's claim
Says why the code does not support the owner's claim that a helper escapes the input

evals.name: diff-review-staged
evals.prompt: A fixture app is already prepared at <app>: a git repo whose baseline commit is clean and whose STAGED changes (git add, uncommitted) add a single new file, src/routes/lookup.js. The user says: "scan my staged changes for security issues before I commit". Save the final chat answer you would give the user to <outputs>/answer.md.
evals.expected_output: An in-chat answer naming the SQL injection in src/routes/lookup.js. The skill writes no files: no report and no threat model; it offers to create the threat model.
expectations: answer.md names the SQL injection (or injection family) in src/routes/lookup.js
answer.md does not claim a full audit was run
<app>/docs/security/ does not exist (a diff review writes no files)
answer.md says there is no threat model yet and offers to create it
The staged file src/routes/lookup.js is unchanged (the skill never edits target code)
substance_expectations: Names the SQL injection in src/routes/lookup.js
Does not report issues in files the staged change does not touch as findings of this change

evals.name: no-subagents
evals.prompt: Run a full security audit of the billing service in <input> (explicit request). The agent-launching (subagent) tool is UNAVAILABLE in this session: treat any launch attempt as an error, retry once at most, and do not work around it by other means. Work ON A COPY: cp -r <input> to <outputs>/app and run the review there. Save the final chat answer you would give the user to <outputs>/answer.md.
evals.expected_output: Validation runs one finding at a time in context; the report says validation was not isolated; the critical SQL injection is not refuted.
expectations: The report header says validation was not isolated and why (no subagents)
The CWE-89 finding in src/routes/admin_users.js is CONFIRMED or LIKELY, not a false positive
The parameterized query in src/routes/products.js is not a confirmed finding
substance_expectations: Names SQL injection in src/routes/admin_users.js
Does not call the parameterized query in src/routes/products.js an SQL injection
